title: Electrification or construction
description: New grid connections, new buildings, or expanded roads could add light.
investigate: Who could say whether connections or building changed here, and over what years?

title: Lighting technology or public-lighting policy changed
description: A switch to LED street lights, longer lighting hours, or a new lighting rule can change recorded brightness — up or down — without a change in activity.
investigate: Were street lights replaced, or did lighting hours change, during this period?

title: Power outage, disaster, conflict, or recovery
description: A dip followed by a rise could reflect disruption and recovery rather than steady growth.
investigate: Did anything interrupt power or daily life in the year of the dip?

title: Seasonal or temporary activity
description: Harvests, festivals, temporary camps, or construction sites can be bright for part of a year and still raise the annual value.
investigate: Is light here steady through the year, or concentrated in certain months?

title: Vehicle lights, fires, or other non-settlement light sources
description: Highways, industrial sites, gas flares, and fires can all be recorded as night-time light.
investigate: What lies inside the grid cells that changed most — homes, a road, a factory?

title: Limited data coverage or processing difference
description: Years with few cloud-free nights, or a change in product version or correction method, can shift values on their own.
investigate: How many valid observations support each year, and did the processing change?
